page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, clocked at 2.55 GHz. Compute capacity consists of 1 dedicated physical core mapped across 2 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside AVX and BMI2, though AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB total, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware acceleration is absent, with no GPUs attached to the instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng (2685.48), with single-threaded compression and decompression maintaining average scores. However, the limited core count places multi-core metrics in the bottom percentiles, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 2691.38 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 1797.0. Large-block memory bandwidth is weak at 29.51 GB/sec for read and 16.11 GB/sec for write operations. Specialized throughput measures such as Redis SET operations (2.1 million ops/sec) and PassMark database operations also track in lower tiers.

The ecs.c7a.large provides an entry-tier footprint for workloads prioritizing single-threaded execution without high concurrency demands. The constrained memory footprint and low baseline network bandwidth limit suitability for memory-intensive data stores or parallel compile jobs. Optimal workloads include lightweight web services, small microservices, and modest single-threaded task workers.

Operating under KVM virtualization, it provides 32 MB of L3 cache, standard instruction sets such as AES and AVX, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The machine contains no bundled local storage and lacks GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-core raw CPU execution alongside average decompression and text processing. However, due to its dual-vCPU count, multi-core benchmarks, database operations, and memory bandwidth score in lower percentiles. The instance serves cost-efficient, entry-level compute requirements such as lightweight web servers, basic microservices, and single-threaded background worker tasks.
